ecosystem.notes: No filing reports App Store volume, so measure is null and the figure sits in studies[]. The study was paid for by Apple ('Support for this study was provided by Apple'), published June 2026 and covers calendar 2025; Apple's fiscal 2026 ran from September 28, 2025 to September 26, 2026, so the periods overlap by about three months only. Its Table 1 total is $1,437B ('more than $1.4 trillion'). About 79% of it ($1,137B) is physical goods and services bought through apps (general retail, travel, food delivery and pickup, grocery, ride hailing and digital payment, the last $16B), on which Apple takes no commission, and about 10% ($151B) is in-app advertising, so it is not App Store sales; digital goods and services are $149B (10%). The study says its estimates 'may not be directly comparable to previous reports'. The 90% no-commission claim is kept with value null (it is a percentage). The study does not state developer earnings or payouts. platformRevenue is null because Apple's FY2026 10-K does not break out App Store revenue: it is inside Services net sales, and the 10-K says 'the Company accounts for all third-party application–related sales on a net basis by recognizing in Services net sales only the commission it retains' (FY2026 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019326000026/aapl-20260926.htm).
